lay.how: The close scene drawn a second time, as a layer on the globe (the globe side of the handover). dive, rise: shares of the dive over which the place comes in and of the rise over which it goes (the storm is small in frame then); the shown plates of the globe, the cirrus of the layer and the clearing of the old cirrus use that ramp. tone: camera heights in radii between which the coarse light of the close view grows in (none, full), even in the log of the height: the layer's ground comes in with it, and the plates (stored without that light) are multiplied by their tone map by that share raised to lightPower, the layer's ground divided by the share that is left (patches.json place.tone). The layer's ground is shown through the inverse of the globe's near grade by the share the grade is not in yet, so it has the globe's look while the globe has it; its cirrus is not, white cloud stays white. nearDeg: arc from the point under the fitted camera inside which the layer always shows (full, gone). edge: feather at the edge of the wide canvas, in camera heights of the close view, measured from the planes through the fitted camera that bound the canvas; wide while the camera is high (first value, above the first of edgeHeight in radii), narrow near the fitted height (second value, below the second of edgeHeight), because near the handover the frame fills with ground close to the canvas border. graze: beyond the near zone the layer shows where the present view is about as grazing as the fitted one (ratio of the sines of elevation, full and gone). texels: and where the canvas keeps this many texels per pixel in its worst direction (gone, full); coreEdge: the finer core canvas counts for that measure only this far inside its border (share of its width), so the measure has no step where the core ends. edgeRange: beyond this distance from the fitted camera (camera heights) the feather grows in proportion to the distance, so far away it is a constant angle of the fitted view. cloudEdge: the cirrus of the layer is drawn wherever the canvas has it, at any height and from any side (it is a thing in the scene), with this feather at the canvas border in units of the tangent of the fitted view; cloudDeg: arc from the point under the fitted camera within which that cirrus is drawn (full, gone), beyond it the canvas has thin streaks near its horizon, which laid back from above are long straight lines; they come in with the honest view instead. cloudBox: left, right and bottom of the part of the canvas whose cirrus is drawn that way, as tangents of the fitted view (the canvas itself is 0.834 wide each way, the frame 0.476): right of 0.6 the wide canvas holds the thin tail of the right bank, 3.2 to 3.7 camera heights away and 12 degrees under the fitted camera, which from above is a fan of straight lines (seen at 4736 and 4744). ground: camera heights in radii between which the ground of the layer comes in (none, full), even in the log of the height. Above the first the plates of the globe alone carry the ground: they hold the same deck laid back, with its dark foreground mended (patches.json place.tone), where the canvas itself has values of 1 to 12 of 255 that cannot be shown lifted. By the second the close view's light is nearly all in and the canvas is shown as it is. settle: heights between which the whole canvas of the close view comes in (ground and cirrus, also where the view from above stretches it) and the lens compensation goes to the close side's. glow: camera heights in radii between which the limb is handed over, even in the log of the height (first value: the globe's Air alone, in the sky and over the ground; second value: the limb glow of the close view alone), so the sky and the limb follow one law of the height on both sides of the handover, in the dive and in the rise. limb, limbRim: the rows of the canvas just under its horizon are the limb of the close view, air seen edge on, not ground: laid on the ground they grow into a wide blue band as the camera rises. So on the globe side the rows under the limb are drawn as the camera of the handover saw them: a ray takes the picture of the ray of that camera that passes the centre of the planet at the same distance in the same compass direction. At the handover that is the close view itself, so nothing changes there; above it the limb keeps its depth in radii and thins on screen as the camera leaves. limb: depth of the ray under the limb in radii down to which that holds in full, and where it has gone. limbRim: the ground of the canvas ends at this depth under its own horizon (radii); the ground beyond takes the pale haze found there, not the blue line. At the handover all ground that this changes lies inside the first value of limb. distant: air between the low camera and the far ground of the globe, a thing in the scene that follows the slant of the view at each point of the ground, not one colour across the frame. While the camera is low the ground seen at a slant is drawn from a coarse level of the globe's map (texels: the width of that level) and mixed towards the air colour (air, times the cloud light and the tint) by veil, so the far ground beside the place is pale and soft like the far ground of the close view and the arcs of the globe do not come in at once when the layer goes. slant: cosine of the angle between the view and the ground's normal below which that holds in full, and above which not at all, so ground seen from straight above is never touched. height: camera heights in radii (none, full), even in the log of the height. dive, rise: amount in the dive and in the rise; 0 in the dive, because there the plates and the canvas disagree on the far ground left of the canvas border and the soft globe shows that as a pale block with a straight edge (4741 to 4750). Never in the ending of the rise, never in the hold, the terrain or the travel.
